item.research_question: How does thermomechanical processing (TMP) tune the microstructure and room-temperature tensile properties of a Co-rich Co35Cr25Ni15Mn15Fe10 (at%) TRIP-HEA?
item.processing_route: High-frequency induction melting and casting; forging at 1473 K; solution treatment at 1473 K for 4 h followed by water quenching (AS); hot-rolling at 1473 K to 50% reduction (HR); warm-rolling at 973 K to 50% reduction (WR); cold-rolling at 293 K to 50% reduction followed by heat treatment at 973 K for 30 min (HT1) or 1023 K for 30 min (HT2)
item.test_conditions: Room temperature (293 K) tensile tests at a strain rate of 1 × 10−3 s−1; Vickers hardness measurement with 500 g load for 15 s
key_findings: Grain size was refined from 144.4 μm in the as-solutionized (AS) sample to 1.83 μm in the HT1 sample.
Yield strength increased from 254.6 MPa (AS) to 641.3 MPa (HT2), and ultimate tensile strength increased from 702.5 MPa (AS) to 968.4 MPa (HT2).
Tensile elongation of the HT2 sample retained a satisfactory value of 68.8% despite the significant strength increase.
Nanosized Cr-rich σ-phase precipitates formed in HT samples with a volume fraction of 0.413% (HT1) and 0.681% (HT2).
The average size of precipitates was 118.8 nm for HT1 and 89 nm for HT2.
Precipitation strengthening contribution (Δσp) was estimated at 10.5 MPa for HT1 and 17.9 MPa for HT2.
Grain boundary strengthening contribution (Δσg) was calculated as 323.9 MPa for HT1 and 247.6 MPa for HT2.
The WR sample exhibited the lowest strain-hardening rate, which decreased rapidly with increasing strain.
item.mechanism: Grain refinement is the primary mechanism for enhancing strength while retaining ductility, whereas nanosized incoherent precipitates provide a dual effect: they refine grains via Smith–Zener drag and block dislocation motion via Orowan strengthening, though they slightly sacrifice ductility.
item.limitations: The formation of incoherent precipitates inevitably sacrifices ductility, which needs to be considered for optimizing TMPs.
item.future_work: The authors state that the results provide guidelines for fabricating high-performance materials and insights into the regulation of microstructure and mechanical properties of TRIP-HEAs, but do not explicitly list specific future experiments.
quotes: The results showed that grain refinement is an effective strategy for enhancing strength while retaining satisfactory ductility.
The formation of incoherent precipitates slightly improves the strength but inevitably sacrifices the ductility, which needs to be considered for optimizing the TMPs.

The room temperature tensile yield strength and ultimate tensile strength were increased from 254.6 to 641.3 MPa and from 702.5 to 968.4 MPa, respectively, but the tensile elongation retains a satisfactory value of 68.8%.
